body:
I think your initial instinct were correct @shannonbooth 

If we *never* touch this field for synchronous navigations, then maybe the rest falls out on its own?

I think this PR also fixes two problems that [#12519](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12519) introduced, which aren't mentioned in the description:

**[Navigate to a fragment](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate-fragid) step 5.1 aborts the navigation it belongs to.**

### Problem 1
- Step 4 fires the navigate event. If the page intercepts it, *navigation*'s [ongoing `navigate` event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigate-event) is that event, and it stays set until the handlers settle.
- Step 5.1 then calls [set the ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-ongoing-navigation). Its step 2 calls [inform the navigation API about aborting navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inform-the-navigation-api-about-aborting-navigation), which aborts the ongoing navigate event. That is the event just intercepted.
- Result: every intercepted fragment navigation fires `navigateerror` and rejects with `AbortError`.

### Problem 2
Nothing clears the ID that step 5.1 stores. A later `window.stop()` or `document.open()` aborts whatever navigate event is ongoing at that time.

### Bot analysis
One WPT consequence: under this PR a traversal intercepted with a precommit handler has its ongoing navigation reset to null once the navigate event returns "canceled-by-navigate". 

So `window.stop()` during the precommit phase still doesn't abort it, which matches [#6905](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6905) and the current text. `navigation-api/precommit-handler/precommitHandler-traversal-window-stop-before-commit.html` expects the opposite; that's [web-platform-tests/wpt#64391](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/issues/64391).

Added the above bot analysis because I think this is argument for test exclusion for interop 2026 for precommitHandler-window-stop-before-commit.html as well

> I think your initial instinct were correct @shannonbooth
> 
> If we _never_ touch this field for synchronous navigations, then maybe the rest falls out on its own?

sorry @theIDinside, I missed this comment! I _think_ that minimal change seems to work for the specific test case reported in #12861, however the realisation that I came to was that the current use of ongoing navigation seems flawed verses how IPC of that field should be happening in an implementation / races itself in the spec, and I think it explains a lot of the issues I have been running into (e.g #12832). So this is trying to take a stab at fixing that.

> I think this PR also fixes two problems that https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12519 introduced, which aren't mentioned in the description:

oh cool, good sign! I wasn't considering those cases when looking at this. I should also (re?)mention here, perhaps indicated a little with my comment I made above and the comment left on the issue itself - I am unconfident in the changes here being 100% correct, but I am fairly confident in it being directionally closer to reality. I'm finding it quite hard to separate this with other specification issues, navigation is a bit of a landmine of complexity. I've been trying to report / focus on standalone issues that are quite self contained / simpler to tackle, but I believe ongoing navigation needs some larger changes. 

one question I do have for yourself / @farre that I ran into when looking at some other issues after I raised this, but regarding this snippet on #12861:

> From the Gecko side of things, we pass this mainly because we don't implement step 19 of [#navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate), and to be honest, I'm not sure that we set [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) to "traversal" for fragment navigations either

I was actually considering at one point whether "traversal" should be part of ongoing navigation at all. Does Gecko model that? This was a while ago and my memory is a bit fuzzy, but https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/embedded-content/the-iframe-element/iframe-loading-lazy-reload-navigation-reload.html was the case I was looking at seemed to suggest to me that a navigation needs to be able to supersede an in flight reload/traversal for the test to be deterministic (which would align with that quoted snippet above of not doing that  I believe). The "nullness" of it seems to be what is most important for superseding navigations, and traversal perhaps mostly relating to this spec snippet:

> Through their [user interface](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nav-traversal-ui), user agents also allow stopping traversals, i.e. cases where the [ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) is "traversal". The above algorithm does not account for this. (On the other hand, user agents do not allow [window.stop()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-window-stop) to stop traversals, so the above algorithm is correct for that caller.) See [issue #6905](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6905).

Which should probably be gated on user involvement (also meaning this is only done from browser process) instead of the broad traversal check. Maybe you also have some insight here @noamr?

will try and take another pass at this on the weekend, I need to refresh my memory a little bit, have spent a little time away from navigation.

<details><summary>(AI-assisted design review)</summary>

Proposed fixes for defects D1, D2, and D3 aren't applied yet. Question Q1 is open.

New in this review:

- D1: `process navigate event handler failure` clears `ongoing navigation` *after* firing `navigateerror`. If a `navigateerror` listener starts a new navigation (e.g. `location.href = "/fallback"`), its new `navigation ID` is immediately overwritten to `null`, causing the second navigation to abort in `navigate` or `process a navigate response`. Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/1f73669) (clear `ongoing navigation` before `Abort a NavigateEvent`, matching `navigatesuccess`).

- D2: `afterPotentialUnloads` step 2 clears `ongoing navigation` whenever `update-only` is false and `ongoing navigation` is *any* `navigation ID`. For a cross-document `push`/`replace` navigation, if `pageswap` (or a task queued before unload) starts a new navigation `navId2`, `afterPotentialUnloads` step 2 overwrites `navId2` to `null` and aborts it. Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/407e3f5) (clear `ongoing navigation` when equal to `navigationId` at the end of `#process-a-navigate-response` and `navigate to a javascript: URL`, and remove `afterPotentialUnloads` step 2).

- D3: The new note under `ongoing navigation` states that it is only ever read or written from tasks on `navigable`'s active window's event loop, but `navigate` steps 9–10 and `navigate to a fragment` step 6.1 still read/write it synchronously from cross-origin callers (`iframe.src = ...`) or `in parallel` (`object`, `embed`, `multipart/x-mixed-replace`). Not applied: [proposed fix](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/6454e4e) (qualify the note).

- Q1: When should `ongoing navigation` be `"traversal"` vs a `navigation ID` vs `null` during `reload()` and `checking if unloading is canceled`? Setting `"traversal"` before `beforeunload`/`navigate` breaks `window.stop()` on intercepted `reload()` and traversals, blocks `e.preventDefault(); location.href = ...` and `location.reload(); location.href = ...`, aborts prior navigations if `beforeunload` cancels, and contradicts 4 existing WPTs; also `afterPotentialUnloads` step 1 unconditionally clears `"traversal"` even if an intercepted fragment navigation replaced it with a `navigation ID`.
  - option a: Only set `"traversal"` in `apply the history step`, and guard `afterPotentialUnloads` step 1 with `ongoing navigation` is `"traversal"` — [spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/166cf51). Minimal diff matching pre-PR behavior; fixes `beforeunload` cancelation, `e.preventDefault(); location.href = ...`, `location.reload(); location.href = ...`, and `precommitHandler-traversal-commit-new-navigation-before-commit.html`, while leaving `window.stop()` on `back()`/`reload()` `precommitHandler`s unaddressed (#6905 / web-platform-tests/wpt#64391).
  - option b: Track `reload()` and `checking if unloading is canceled`'s `navigate` event with a fresh `navigation ID`, and only set `"traversal"` in `apply the history step` (with `afterPotentialUnloads` step 1 guarded) — [spec](https://github.com/noamr/html/commit/d55ce4c). Fixes all 4 regressions and makes all 4 contradicting WPTs pass; slightly more spec text than option a.
  - option c: Keep as is and update the 4 contradicting WPTs.

  <details><summary>Contradicting WPTs</summary>

  - `navigation-api/precommit-handler/precommitHandler-window-stop-before-commit.html` (subtest 4: `precommitHandler with window.stop() before reload commit`)
  - `navigation-api/precommit-handler/precommitHandler-traversal-commit-new-navigation-before-commit.html`
  - `navigation-api/precommit-handler/precommitHandler-traversal-window-stop-before-commit.html`
  - `navigation-api/navigate-event/signal-abort-window-stop-same-document.html` (subtest: `window.stop() inside a navigate listener aborts a cancelable traversal`)

  </details>

<details><summary>Earlier thread concerns</summary>

- `same-document-nav-cross-document-nav.html` (#12861): addressed in `df49fcd` (`update-only` is true for synchronous same-document updates, preserving the subsequent `navigation ID`).
- theIDinside's [comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12942#issuecomment-6126251682): synchronous same-document updates are skipped via `update-only`, while `navigate to a fragment` still needs `navigationId` when intercepted so `window.stop()` can abort it.
- shannonbooth's [review comment](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12942#discussion_r4007177040): keeping `documentState`/`historyEntry`/`navigationParams` creation in the queued task on `navigable`'s active window is needed because it reads `navigable`'s active document / target name on that event loop.

</details>

Reviewed at df49fcd on d2f752f, using spec-pr-review.
</details>
